title: Paytm gets RBI’s in-principle nod for wallet licence
summary:
One 97 Communications’ wholly owned subsidiary Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL) has received in-principle authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to issue and operate prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.
In a regulatory filing, Paytm said the RBI granted the approval on November 13 under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The authorisation is subject to compliance with RBI’s Master Directions on Prepaid Payment Instruments.
PPSL will have to complete a system audit, including a cybersecurity audit, and submit the report to the RBI within six months. Failure to meet the deadline will result in the automatic lapse of the in-principle authorisation.
The company can commence issuing prepaid payment instruments only after receiving the final authorisation or Certificate of Authorisation from the central bank.
Paytm had applied for a fresh PPI licence through PPSL in July 2026, marking its first formal step towards reviving its wallet business after the RBI cancelled the banking licence of Paytm Payments Bank in April 2026.
The company disclosed the application in its June-quarter investor presentation, saying that a wallet would add to the completeness of its consumer payments offerings. It also said consumers benefit from having multiple payment options.
The wallet business was earlier operated through Paytm Payments Bank. Following regulatory restrictions imposed on the bank in 2024, customers were barred from adding money to their wallets, although existing balances could be withdrawn.
The RBI cancelled the bank's licence on April 24, 2026, citing non-compliance with licensing conditions and regulatory requirements. The central bank also said the bank's affairs and management were detrimental to depositors' interests and public interest.
The latest in-principle approval brings Paytm a step closer to restoring its wallet offering under PPSL. However, the company will need the RBI's final authorisation before it can resume issuing wallets.

title: Haber crosses Rs 200 Cr revenue threshold in FY26, narrows losses by 53%
summary:
Industrial automation company Haber’s revenue growth outpaced the increase in its overall expenses in FY26, helping the company reduce its net loss by more than half during the last fiscal year. 
The firm’s revenue from operations rose 38.7% to Rs 215 crore in FY26 from Rs 155 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). 


Haber generates revenue from product sales, mainly chemicals supplied alongside software-enabled industrial solutions.
Product sales remained the main source of revenue, contributing nearly 97% of the company’s operating income. Revenue from this segment increased 37.4% to Rs 209.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 152.5 crore a year earlier. 
The company also supplies chemicals alongside software-enabled industrial solutions, with product sales accounting for most of its business. Revenue from services, meanwhile, grew 81.7% to Rs 5.27 crore in FY26.
Haber earned another Rs 18 crore in other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 233 crore in FY26, against Rs 167 crore in FY25. This additional income contributed to the overall financial performance, though operating revenue remained the larger component of its income.
On the cost side, materials consumed continued to account for the biggest share of expenses. This item rose 40% to Rs 133 crore in FY26 from Rs 95 crore in the previous year, mainly tracking the growth in product sales. Employee benefit expenses increased 52% to Rs 38 crore from Rs 25 crore, while site labour and supervision contract costs grew 21.4% to Rs 17 crore.
Other operating costs also moved up. Transportation expenses increased 13.6% to Rs 10 crore, while depreciation rose 17% to Rs 11 crore. Finance costs edged up 4.3% to Rs 10 crore. In contrast, other expenses fell 11% to Rs 26 crore from Rs 29.21 crore in FY25.
The combined effect of these cost movements kept the increase in total expenses below revenue growth. Haber’s total expenses rose 28.3% to Rs 245 crore in FY26 from Rs 191 crore a year earlier. The slower growth in expenses helped narrow the gap between the company’s income and expenditure, contributing to a reduction in its net loss to Rs 11.24 crore.
Its EBITDA margin improved to -4.48% in FY26 from -10.53% in FY25. On a unit basis, Haber spent Rs 1.14 for every rupee of operating revenue. While the company was yet to bring its spending below operating revenue, the change indicated better cost control.
Haber reported current assets of Rs 398 crore as of March 2026, down from Rs 429 crore a year earlier. However, its cash and bank balances increased to Rs 217 crore from Rs 199 crore in FY25. The company has raised over $70 million to date, including a $44 million Series C round in December 2024.
Haber’s FY26 performance showed an improvement in its operating economics, with revenue growth outpacing expense growth and losses narrowing during the year. The improvement in its EBITDA margin and lower spending per rupee of revenue also pointed to better cost management. The focus now will be on sustaining this progress as the company scales its business and works towards profitability.

title: Kutlerri.ai raises $4 Mn from Narahari Investments to expand AI solutions for restaurants
summary:
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million from Houston-based Narahari Investments.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its AI Catering Sales Agent, launch three other AI agents currently in beta testing and develop a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Co-founded in December last year by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy, Kutlerri.ai is building AI agents to help restaurants improve sales, manage expenses and increase profitability. It follows a performance-linked pricing model, charging customers based on additional revenue generated or costs saved rather than fixed subscription fees.
The startup currently has more than 10 signed customers in the US. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also operates an office in Houston. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Its first commercial product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius, contacts them through emails, texts and calls, and helps restaurants convert enquiries into orders.
The product was developed with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group in the Washington DC region. According to Kutlerri.ai, the agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over 10 months, more than 10 times the amount paid for the service, without hiring additional sales personnel.
The startup currently has one commercially available product, three agents undergoing beta testing and two in development. It plans to expand its teams and launch more products. While the US remains its primary market, Kutlerri.ai is also exploring opportunities in India and other geographies.

title: MeitY examines data collection by home services platforms for physical AI training
summary:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has raised concerns over the collection of first-person video and sensor data from gig workers to train physical AI models. The scrutiny comes amid Pronto’s in-home video recording initiative, while rival platforms Snabbit and Urban Company have decided against adopting the practice.
According to an ET report, senior officials from the ministry met representatives of home services platforms, including Snabbit, Pronto and Urban Company, along with technology and robotics companies on Thursday to discuss concerns around workers’ rights, consumer privacy and data sovereignty.
The meeting, chaired by MeitY secretary S Krishnan, sought details on standard operating procedures (SOPs) for collecting, processing and storing first-person video recordings. The ministry also asked companies about safeguards to obtain workers’ consent and protect the privacy of household members and other individuals captured in the footage.
Companies were also questioned on whether the data collected was being sold, shared or transferred to AI developers outside India. The ministry sought disclosures on data-sharing agreements, vendor contracts, retention policies and the nature and scale of information being collected.
Among the three home services platforms, Pronto has started in-home video recording through its Verified service. Snabbit and Urban Company have ruled out adopting the practice. According to ET, Pronto has been asked to submit a detailed representation on its data collection practices and SOPs.
Some executives at the meeting also raised concerns about collecting data in India and selling it to overseas physical AI developers, arguing that the practice does not put the country in a favourable position. Robotics startups also suggested that India should focus on developing domestic physical AI capabilities rather than supplying training data to overseas companies.
In a statement, Pronto said it participated in the MeitY consultation as part of a broader industry discussion on responsible data practices. The company said data generated through its customer booking journey involves customer consent and can support downstream AI applications. It added that its existing practices are designed to comply with applicable regulations and that it would continue to engage with the ministry as the policy framework evolves.
Pronto’s data collection initiative comes months after the Bengaluru-based startup raised $20 million from US-based tech investor Lachy Groom, co-founder of AI startup Physical Intelligence. Its founder, Anjali Sardana, has also set up a new physical AI venture, Provision Labs, which works with developers building AI models for robotics and other real-world applications.
Investor interest in India’s physical AI ecosystem has also grown. According to an Entrackr report, startups in the segment raised around $155 million across 31 deals as of July 2026, compared with $130 million across 25 deals in 2025.
A separate set of companies is building the data collection, annotation and training infrastructure required for physical AI systems. Human Archive is developing human sensorimotor datasets for robots, while Neo Cambrian has launched an India-focused robotics data factory. Other companies operating across this segment in India include iMerit, Human Stryde, Luel, Awign, Build, Centific, Humyn Labs, Aura ML, Build AI, FPV Labs and Northstar.
Physical AI models require real-world data that captures human actions, objects, environments and interactions. Much of this data has to be collected specifically for robotics and embodied AI use cases rather than sourced from existing internet datasets.
ET also quoted legal experts highlighting that video recordings, facial images, location traces and sensor data could qualify as personal data when they identify or can reasonably be linked to a worker. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act requires platforms to provide clear notices on data collection and processing purposes, worker rights and grievance mechanisms.
The development follows earlier discussions among startups working on physical AI to establish common standards for worker pay, wellbeing, working hours, safety and legal compliance.

title: Desible.ai raises Rs 32 Cr led by Prime Venture Partners
summary:
Bengaluru-based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine.
The fresh capital will be used towards strengthening its agentic AI capabilities, expanding compliance infrastructure, accelerating product development and scaling sales and marketing operations.
Founded in 2025 by Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, Desible.ai is building an AI-powered workflow orchestration platform for banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and insurance providers.
The platform helps financial institutions automate customer engagement, servicing, collections, underwriting and compliance processes. It initially focused on voice-based automation and is expanding to channels such as WhatsApp, SMS and email.
Desible.ai currently supports more than 25 workflows across revenue generation, risk and compliance, collections, customer service and claims. 
The company claims its platform handles over 10 million customer engagements every month and works with insurance providers, while more than 40 BFSI institutions are using or evaluating its solutions.
Its platform integrates with existing enterprise systems and uses predefined decision-making rules to ensure customer consent, regulatory disclosures and escalation procedures are followed. The compliance framework is aligned with requirements from IRDAI, RBI, TRAI and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

title: Exclusive: Baaz Bikes to kick off Series B round led by BIG Capital
summary:
Full-stack electric vehicle ecosystem for gig workers, Baaz Bikes is set to raise its Series B funding round led by BIG Capital, with participation from existing investor Kalaari Capital and Aravind Sanka.
The company's board has approved the issuance of 6,105 Series B preference shares at an issue price of Rs 75,716 each to raise Rs 46.22 crore, according to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.
BIG Capital will lead the round with an investment of Rs 38 crore, while Kalaari Capital will contribute Rs 8 crore. The remaining amount will be invested by Aravind Sanka. The ongoing Series B round appears to be part of a larger fundraise, with the company likely to bring in additional capital as the round progresses.
According to Entrackr's estimates, the transaction pegs Baaz Bikes' post-money valuation at around Rs 325 crore ($34 million). This valuation could change if the company raises additional capital in the ongoing round.
The fresh proceeds will be used towards capital expenditure, product development, and working capital requirements, as per the company's filings.
Founded by Anubhav Sharma and Shubham Srivastava, Baaz Bikes operates a full-stack electric mobility platform focused on gig workers. The company provides electric scooters on a subscription basis to delivery partners working with platforms such as Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto and Amazon. Its subscription model also covers multiple battery swaps, helping delivery partners avoid the upfront cost of purchasing an electric vehicle.
Baaz Bikes had raised approximately $12 million (around Rs 100 crore) before the current Rs 46.22 crore Series B round, including its July 2025 extended Series A funding.
The company is building its business around the growing demand for electric two-wheelers in the last-mile delivery segment, where delivery partners depend on affordable and reliable mobility solutions.

title: Bodhi Tree to acquire majority stake in restaurant chain A2B for $180 Mn
summary:
Chennai-based restaurant chain A2B (Adyar Ananda Bhavan) has entered into a $180 million deal with Bodhi Tree Systems, which will acquire a majority stake in the company.
Announced on November 12, the partnership will focus on expanding A2B’s operations across India and international markets. The investors also plan to strengthen the company’s management structure and prepare it for a potential stock market listing.
Founded nearly five decades ago, A2B has grown from a sweet shop into a food services business with around 160 outlets in India and over 30 locations overseas. The company employs more than 15,000 people and has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Its business spans restaurants, sweets, savouries and packaged food products.
Following the transaction, Uday Shankar, co-founder of Bodhi Tree Systems, will become chairman of A2B’s board. Bodhi Tree is an investment platform backed by James Murdoch’s Lupa Systems and Uday Shankar.
The partnership will focus on investments in technology, operational efficiencies and business capabilities, alongside strengthening A2B’s management team. It will also work towards making the company ready for a potential public listing.
Commenting on the development, A2B co-founder K T Srinivasa Raja said the business, which he started with his brother as a sweet shop 50 years ago, has become a part of everyday life for millions of families. He added that the partnership with Bodhi Tree would provide the resources and capabilities needed to support the company’s next phase of growth.
Murdoch and Shankar cited A2B’s brand recognition, consumer trust and international presence as key factors behind the investment.
Outside India, A2B operates in Singapore, the US, Australia, Malaysia and the UK.

Other expenses grew 3.4% to Rs 147.4 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 142.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Overall, the company's total expenses increased 19.2% to Rs 441.5 crore from Rs 370.5 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the bottom line, Wakefit's profit before tax surged 66.3% to Rs 26.54 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 15.96 crore in Q2 FY26.

title: Turtlemint posts Rs 342 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, losses narrow 67%
summary:
Insurance distribution platform Turtlemint announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27. The company reported a 35.2% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net loss narrowed 67.1% to Rs 25.83 crore.
Turtlemint's revenue from operations increased 35.2% year-on-year to Rs 342 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 253 crore in Q2 FY26, according to the company’s financial statements filed with the NSE.
Founded by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates a technology-led platform for the distribution of insurance and other financial products.
The firm also recorded Rs 9.5 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 352 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 255 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Turtlemint's total expenses increased 25% to Rs 375 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 300 crore in Q2 FY26. The company does not disclose a detailed breakup of its expenses in its financial statements.
Among the reported expense heads, other expenses surged 31% to Rs 306.50 crore, while employee benefit expenses rose 4.2% to Rs 64.23 crore. Depreciation expenses stood at Rs 4.30 crore during the quarter.
At the bottom line, Turtlemint narrowed its net loss by 67.1% to Rs 25.83 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 78.45 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), the company's revenue from operations grew 37.6% to Rs 637 crore from Rs 463 crore in H1 FY26. At the same time,  its net losses narrowed down by 50.9% to Rs 61.42 crore from Rs 125 crore in the corresponding period last year.
On Thursday, Turtlemint shares closed at Rs 61.13 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 1,800 crore.

title: MGF-Kavachh leads Rs 18 Cr seed round in climate startup mistEO
summary:
Thiruvananthapuram-based climate intelligence startup mistEO has raised Rs 18 crore in a seed funding round led by MGF-Kavachh, with participation from Seafund and other investors.
The funding was announced at HUDDLE GLOBAL 2026, the eighth edition of the event.
The startup will use the proceeds to scale its flagship Climate Decision Intelligence (CDI) platform for banks, insurers and agricultural value chains across India and Asia.
Founded in 2019 by Samuel John and Ambarish Narayanan, mistEO combines weather modelling with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to convert weather and climate data into actionable insights.
Its CDI platform integrates satellite, radar, Internet of Things (IoT) and ground-sensor data to help financial institutions and businesses assess the impact of weather events on farms, assets and loans.
The company’s proprietary forecasting model, Indra, provides weather forecasts at a spatial resolution of 3 km across three time windows: 0-6 hours, 6-24 hours and 24-48 hours.
mistEO also develops solutions for maritime operations, renewable energy forecasting, logistics and mobility, and flood and heavy-rainfall monitoring.
In India, the startup works with NABARD and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on the DiCRA initiative, which provides climate resilience data for agriculture. In Australia, its livestock early warning system helps cattle farmers prepare for heat stress up to seven days in advance.
The startup is also working with the Indian Air Force on a thunderstorm nowcasting model under the iDEX programme. It is developing early warning systems for the Indian Navy as well.
Incubated at Social Alpha, mistEO is headquartered in Thiruvananthapuram and also operates an office in Melbourne, Australia. It plans to strengthen its forecasting and risk models, expand its team and build partnerships across Asian markets.

title: Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 revenue dips 39% to Rs 421 Cr; cuts losses by 13%
summary:
After witnessing a prolonged slowdown over the past eight quarters, electric vehicle maker Ola Electric continued to face pressure on its business in Q2 FY27, with revenue declining 39% year-on-year. However, the Bengaluru-based company managed to narrow its losses by 13%.
Ola Electric’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 421 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 690 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.

The company's automotive business generated Rs 420 crore, while its cell business contributed Rs 3 crore during the quarter, before inter-segment eliminations of Rs 2 crore. During the quarter, Ola Electric recorded 41,650 EV registrations, a 17% year-on-year decline.
Apart from operating revenue, the company reported Rs 27 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 448 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 896 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, the company’s revenue from operations fell over 7% from Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27.
The decline in revenue was accompanied by a reduction in procurement costs, which fell 38% YoY to Rs 295 crore in Q2 FY27. However, employee benefit cost rose 22% to Rs 67 crore. Overall, Ola Electric’s total expenses fell 31% to Rs 810 crore from Rs 1,174 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Overall, Ola Electric’s total expenses fell 31% to Rs 810 crore from Rs 1,174 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Despite lower sales and a decline in revenue, Ola Electric managed to narrow its losses by 13% year-on-year to Rs 362 crore in Q2 FY27. The decline in procurement costs, which fell 38% to Rs 295 crore, helped the company reduce its overall expenses and limit losses during the quarter.
For the first half of FY27, Ola Electric’s revenue declined 42% to Rs 876 crore, while its losses also narrowed down 17.5% to Rs 698 crore.
Meanwhile, rival Ather Energy reported a contrasting performance, with revenue from operations surging 63% year-on-year to Rs 1,464 crore in Q2 FY27. The company also turned profitable during the quarter.
According to Vahan data, Ola Electric ranked fifth among EV two-wheeler players with 12,096 registrations and a 5.4% market share. It was the only player among the top five to record a month-on-month decline, with registrations falling 10.12% from 13,458 units in September.
Ahead of its Q2 FY27 results, Ola Electric raised Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue to strengthen its capital position amid continued pressure. At the end of Thursday’s trading session, Ola Electric shares closed 3.8% higher at Rs 35.74 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 16,542 crore ($1.74 billion).

title: Norwest closes $4 Bn global fund, takes AUM to $18 Bn
summary:
Global investment firm Norwest has closed its latest fund, Norwest 18, at $4 billion, the largest fundraise in the firm's 65-year history. The close takes its total assets under management (AUM) to $18 billion.
The fund will support venture capital and growth equity investments across the technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel. Norwest's portfolio includes companies such as Babylist, Gong, Monogram Health, OfBusiness, VAST Data, Vuori and YipitData.
Since launching its previous fund, Norwest 17, in April 2024, the firm has made more than 87 investments. It has also supported over 30 portfolio companies in achieving liquidity events through public listings and strategic acquisitions.
Companies from its portfolio that went public during this period include India's Amagi Media Labs and Swiggy, along with BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences and Omada Health. Several portfolio companies were also acquired, including Avetta by EQT, AbsenceSoft by Luminate Capital Partners, Ouro Medicines by Gilead Sciences, Qualified by Salesforce, tvScientific by Pinterest and Veza by ServiceNow.
Norwest is expanding its investment focus into areas such as next-generation financial infrastructure, physical and voice AI, agentic cybersecurity, technology-enabled industrial and aerospace businesses, and healthcare AI.
Its recent investments in financial infrastructure include Beltic, Rain and Stablecore, while Coval, Generalist AI and LlamaIndex are among its investments in AI systems and agentic technologies.
In cybersecurity, the firm has backed Above Security, ORION Security, Red Access and Zenity. Its investments in industrial and aerospace businesses include East Range Group, Padmini VNA, JJG Aerospace and Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group.
The firm has also invested in healthcare companies such as Infinx, Matchpoint Therapeutics, Rezo Therapeutics, Tokaido Health and Vitalize Care, which are applying technology and AI across drug discovery, clinical workflows and healthcare delivery.
Beyond funding, Norwest provides portfolio companies with strategic advisory and operational support. It has expanded its Portfolio Success platform by doubling its Senior Advisor Network, adding Operating Executives and launching the Norwest Operator Collective and Norwest Kinetic.
Founded in 1961, Norwest has invested in more than 750 companies and currently partners with over 275 businesses across its venture and growth equity portfolio. The firm has offices in Menlo Park and San Francisco in California, Mumbai in India, and Tel Aviv in Israel.

title: Neeman’s revenue jumps 73% to Rs 180 Cr in FY26, losses narrow 30%
summary:
Sneakers have evolved beyond footwear into markers of identity and self-expression, shaped by basketball and hip-hop culture since the 1980s. In India, however, the market remained dominated by global brands such as Nike, Adidas and Puma, leaving limited room for homegrown labels.
That is beginning to change as sneaker culture gains traction among Indian consumers. Brands such as Neeman’s, Comet, Gully Labs and Snitch are entering the space with distinct designs, pricing and brand identities, seeking to build homegrown alternatives.
The shift has also caught investors’ attention, with funding flowing into the emerging category as homegrown brands look to tap into growing consumer interest in sneakers.
Among the early homegrown brands to tap into this shift was Neeman’s, which reported a 73% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 180 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 104 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

Founded in 2017 by Taranjeet Singh Chhabra and Amar Preet Singh, Neeman’s follows a direct-to-consumer (D2C) model and focuses on comfortable footwear made using sustainable materials. Its portfolio now includes sneakers, loafers, flip-flops, slides, and sandals 
The sale of footwear remains the company's only source of operating revenue. Apart from its core business, Neeman’s also earned around Rs 3 crore, largely through net gains on investments. This pushed its total income to Rs 183 crore in FY26, against Rs 107 crore in the previous fiscal.
For a footwear brand, materials and manufacturing costs naturally take up a significant share of the overall expenses. At Neeman’s, material procurement alone accounted for 38% of its total expenditure. In line with the scale of operations, this cost increased 58.3% to Rs 76 crore in FY26 from Rs 48 crore in FY25.
The firm's employee benefit cost stood at Rs 19.43 crore, while advertising and marketing expenses jumped 57.1% to Rs 45 crore during the year. Legal, technology, finance, travel and other overheads also added to the bill, taking Neeman’s overall expenditure up 53.1% to Rs 199 crore in FY26.
Interestingly, while the company's revenue grew 73%, its overall expenses increased at a slower pace. This helped Neeman narrow its losses by 30.4% to Rs 16 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23 crore in the previous fiscal.
On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.11 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin also improved to -28.46% and -7.21%, respectively.

Neeman’s has raised around $17 million in funding to date, with investors such as Grand Anicut and Sharrp Ventures. The broader sneaker category is also attracting investor interest. Comet recently secured a Rs 100 crore led by Verlinvest, while Gully Labs kicked off its Series A round this year.
India’s sneaker market is moving beyond its niche roots, with younger consumers embracing new designs, collaborations and limited-edition releases. Homegrown brands have an opportunity to build on this interest, but consumer excitement alone will not guarantee lasting biz. Their challenge will be to convert first-time buyers into repeat customers, maintain product relevance and build viable economics as competition increases. 
Will India's sneaker obsession continue to grow, creating room for more homegrown brands, or will the category eventually settle into a more conventional lifestyle business with modest growth?

title: Exclusive: Dhruva Space to raise $15.5 Mn in pre-Series B; revenue surges 8X
summary:
Spacetech startup Dhruva Space is all set to raise Rs 147 crore (approximately $15.5 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IndusBridge Ventures, with participation from government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and others.
The latest funding follows AVCF’s earlier investment of Rs 60 crore in Dhruva Space in July 2026. With a corpus of over Rs 1,000 crore, AVCF was established under the guidance of IN-SPACe and is managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited.
Dhruva Space’s board has approved the issuance of 1,573 pre-Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 9,34,429.47 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
IndusBridge Ventures Fund led the round with an investment of Rs 60 crore, followed by Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), which invested Rs 46.9 crore to increase its stake in the company. Blue Ashva Sampada Fund committed Rs 18.22 crore, while PVS Raju invested Rs 10 crore. The remaining amount came from four other investors.
However, according to the filing, the investments from Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and Akshat Greentech, are yet to be received.
According to Entrackr’s estimates, Dhruva Space will command a post-money valuation of around Rs 2,200 crore (around $230 million).
The company will use the funds to develop and launch communication, earth observation and remote sensing satellites, besides meeting working capital needs, infrastructure development and general corporate expenses, the filing further stated.
Founded by Sanjay Nekkanti, Chaitanya Dora, Krishna Teja Penamakuru and Abhay Egoor, Dhruva Space operates a full-stack spacetech business, offering satellite manufacturing, launch integration and ground station solutions to commercial, government and defence customers. It also provides satellite deployment services and access to space-based data and imagery through its platforms.
Following the allotment, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund will hold a 6.29% stake in the company, while AVCF and IndusBridge Ventures will own 3.32% and 2.73%, respectively. The promoters will collectively retain a 40.74% stake.
Financially, Dhruva Space reported an nearly eightfold jump in operating revenue to Rs 79 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 10 crore in FY25. However, its losses also widened 21% year-on-year to Rs 46.6 crore.
India’s spacetech sector has witnessed a pickup in funding activity, with investors showing growing interest in startups across satellite manufacturing, launch vehicles and space-based data services. The trend also reflects increasing institutional participation and government-backed initiatives to support homegrown space technology companies.
Recently, Skyroot became India’s first spacetech unicorn after raising $60 million in a funding round. Bengaluru-based Pixxel raised $100 million in a Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, while Bellatrix Aerospace secured $20 million in a pre-Series B round. Last year, Digantara and Agnikul raised $50 million and $17 million, respectively.

title: Hundo Pizza raises maiden institutional round led by Titan Capital

Co-founder Kabir Moorjani oversees product development and kitchen operations, while Ronak Rajani, who founded Mumbai Foodie, acquired by Swiggy in 2024, leads growth and marketing.

Founded in 2015, Olyv operates as an online lending marketplace through its website and mobile application. The platform connects borrowers and lenders, offering unsecured loans digitally. The startup’s product portfolio primarily includes small-ticket personal loans catering to micro-merchants, self-employed individuals, small retailers, blue- and grey-collar workers, as well as salaried professionals.
Following the latest allotment, Nippon India Digital holds a 4.53% stake in Olyv, while existing investor Fundamentum owns a 12.47% stake.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Olyv reported a 36% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 338 crore, compared to Rs 249 crore in FY24, while its net profit more than doubled to Rs 26 crore during the same period.

HomeLane provides end-to-end home interior solutions, covering the entire process from home design and contract manufacturing to installation and execution. The company offers customised interior solutions to homeowners through its technology-led platform, with these services remaining its sole source of operating revenue in FY26.
HomeLane contributed Rs 535 crore, accounting for over 72% of the combined revenue in FY26, while its acquired entity Design Cafe added Rs 202 crore. Together, the two businesses generated Rs 738 crore in revenue during the last fiscal year.
The company also earned Rs 7 crore from interest on deposits, taking its total income to Rs 745 crore during the fiscal year.
Despite a decline in material costs, overall expenditure remained high. The cost of materials remained the largest cost component, accounting for 34.3% of total expenses at Rs 302.5 crore in FY26. However, this cost declined 5.5% year-on-year from Rs 320 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses increased 13% to Rs 270 crore, while advertising and marketing costs rose 13.1% to Rs 95 crore during the last fiscal year.
Installation and allied costs declined 26.5% to Rs 61 crore, whereas other expenses, including contract manufacturing charges, legal and professional fees, travel and overheads, increased 9% to Rs 153.5 crore. Overall, HomeLane's total expenses grew 1.7% to Rs 882 crore in FY26 from Rs 867 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Higher employee benefit, advertising and marketing expenses weighed on HomeLane’s bottom line, with losses before tax widening 23.4% to Rs 137 crore during the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 111 crore in FY25.

On a unit basis, HomeLane spent Rs 1.2 to earn a rupee in FY26. Its EBITDA margin worsened to Rs -15.3% whereas EBITDA (loss) stood at Rs 113 crore. As of March 2026, the firm has a total current assets of Rs 209 crore with cash and bank balances of Rs 86 crore.
In an earlier interaction with Entrackr, HomeLane co-founder and CEO Srikanth Iyer said the company has gradually shifted its focus towards profitable growth rather than pursuing growth at any cost. The firm is also working towards improving its operating economics as it integrates Design Cafe and scales its business. Despite reporting losses for FY26, HomeLane turned EBITDA-profitable in Q4 FY26, indicating improved operating performance toward the end of the fiscal year.
"For the last couple of years, our focus has shifted slowly to profitable growth. We want to grow, but we need to grow profitably," Iyer said.
For the ongoing fiscal (FY7), HomeLane is targeting EBITDA profitability of 5-6%, according to Iyer. Over the longer term, the firm aims to scale revenue to around Rs 3,000 crore by FY31, which would require 30-35% annual growth. It’s also evaluating a potential IPO in the coming years.
HomeLane’s next phase will be shaped by its ability to compete in a fragmented home interiors market, where organised players such as Livspace and newer technology-led platforms are vying for a larger share of urban home renovation spending. The challenge is to differentiate through execution, predictable delivery and customer experience, rather than relying only on design tools or wider reach. 
The firm, meanwhile, needs to revive growth after its revenue remained flat in FY26. Its proposed IPO will also depend on its ability to demonstrate consistent growth, stronger margins and a durable business model.

title: Unacademy’s Gaurav Munjal moves to Executive Chairman, CBO Akhilendra Kumar becomes CEO
summary:
Unacademy co-founder and CEO Gaurav Munjal is moving to the role of Executive Chairman, with chief business officer (CBO) Akhilendra Kumar set to take over as the company's new chief executive.
Announcing the leadership transition in a post on X, Munjal said he would remain actively involved in the company's day-to-day operations and work alongside Kumar. He also said he would help with the upGrad IPO.
Kumar is currently the CBO at Unacademy and has been with the company for nearly five years.
The leadership change comes nearly two months after upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy in September 2026 in an all-stock deal valued at just over $200 million. The transaction marked a steep decline from Unacademy's peak valuation of around $3.4 billion in 2021.
The acquisition gives upGrad an entry into the online test preparation segment, including UPSC, JEE, NEET and GATE, while adding Unacademy's educator network to its existing higher education, upskilling and study abroad businesses.
At the time of the acquisition, Munjal said Unacademy had a topline of around Rs 400 crore, with most of its businesses either profitable or near profitable. The company also had around Rs 900 crore in the bank, he added.
On the other hand, upGrad's gross revenue grew 7% year-on-year to Rs 2,070 crore in FY26, including taxes. Its total income stood at Rs 1,732 crore after Ind-AS accounting. The company reported a provisional profit of Rs 38.8 crore during the 11 months ended February 2026.
Following the acquisition, upGrad is also consolidating the operations of Unacademy and its businesses. PrepLadder's headquarters has already been shifted from Chandigarh to Bengaluru, while Unacademy, PrepLadder, Airlearn and Graphy will operate from Bengaluru going forward.

summary:
Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B funding round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund.
The round also saw participation from Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund. Blue Ashva Capital, which led the company’s Series A round in 2021, remains its largest shareholder.
Separately, Greenjoules has secured a Rs 100 crore loan from the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology. The combined Rs 250 crore financing will support the company’s expansion plans.
The proceeds will be deployed to set up a manufacturing facility at Khed City in Pune, with a planned capacity to produce 200,000 litres of biocrude per day from agricultural waste. The facility will be developed in phases, starting in 2027, Greenjoules said in a press release.
Founded in 2018 by S. Viraraghavan, Radhika Viraraghavan, Shweta Viraraghavan and Sethunath Ramaswamy, Greenjoules converts agricultural and agro-industrial waste into renewable fuels using its proprietary Integrated Catalytic Thermocracking (ICTC) technology. Its biocrude is further processed into renewable diesel and bio-naphtha.
The company’s renewable diesel can be used in existing vehicles, engines and fuel infrastructure without modifications. Greenjoules is also exploring applications in sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), green hydrogen and sustainable materials.
India’s renewable fuels sector has attracted investments in companies developing alternatives to conventional fuels using agricultural and organic waste.
In June, Bengaluru-based GPS Renewables secured Rs 635 crore in Series C funding and associated financing to expand its compressed biogas (CBG) infrastructure.
FarmWatt Innovations raised Rs 32.5 crore from IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter to strengthen its biomass collection network, while BiofuelCircle raised Rs 35 crore in a bridge round led by Spectrum Impact to expand its biomass supply chain.

title: Kunal Shah sets three priorities for WhatsApp, but spam and payments remain key challenges
summary:
WhatsApp is looking to expand beyond messaging and make its platform more useful for everyday activities, including bill payments, financial services and bookings. The Meta-owned platform's global head Kunal Shah has outlined three priorities for the app: richer communication, simpler services and artificial intelligence (AI).
In a post on X, Shah said the company wanted to help users stay connected with people who matter to them while allowing them to get more things done through WhatsApp.
The first priority is to improve communication features such as voice notes, groups, stickers and video. Shah said users send over 10 billion voice messages and more than 4 billion stickers on WhatsApp every day. The company wants to make these experiences simpler and more expressive.
The second focus is to make everyday activities as simple as sending a message. Shah cited activities such as paying bills, borrowing money and staying connected while travelling, which often require users to switch between multiple platforms. WhatsApp is working with financial services and telecom partners to simplify these processes.
However, the payments opportunity comes with its own challenges. Despite its large user base and the rollout of UPI payments, WhatsApp Pay has struggled to gain traction in India. It accounted for just 0.8% of UPI transaction volume in September 2026, far behind PhonePe and Google Pay, which together controlled nearly 78% of the market. 
WhatsApp also faces a more immediate problem: spam, particularly from business accounts. Shah's post drew criticism from users on X, who questioned the company's focus on new services and AI while unwanted promotional messages continued to flood their inboxes. A LocalCircles survey in February 2026 found that 96% of WhatsApp users received promotional or spam messages every day. 
This could become a bigger challenge as WhatsApp seeks to expand commerce and financial services on its platform. Building trust will be essential if users are expected to discover businesses and complete transactions through the app.
AI is the third priority. Shah said WhatsApp wants to use the technology to help users find information, complete tasks and keep track of bookings and appointments. He did not share details about specific features or launch timelines.
Shah also said the expansion would not come at the cost of privacy. WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls every day, while personal messages and calls will continue to remain end-to-end encrypted. 
WhatsApp's ambition is to evolve into a broader digital services platform. But its ability to do so will depend not just on adding features, but also on addressing spam and demonstrating that its payments and business services can gain wider adoption.

title: RentoMojo reports first quarterly results post listing, Q2 FY27 revenue grows 53%
summary:
Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo has reported its first quarterly results since listing on the stock exchanges, with its revenue from operations growing 52.69% year-on-year in Q2 FY27. The company also saw its profit before tax (PBT) increase 54% during the quarter.
RentoMojo’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 142 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 93 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 1.6 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 144 crore in Q2 FY27.
RentoMojo operates a rental platform for furniture and home appliances, allowing consumers to access products through monthly subscriptions. Its platform primarily caters to urban households across major Indian cities.
On the cost side, the company's total expenditure increased 53.85% to Rs 120 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 78 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 19.5 crore during the quarter, while finance costs, depreciation and other overheads contributed to the overall expenses.

At the bottom line, RentoMojo's profit before tax increased 54.19% to Rs 24.3 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 15.8 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its net profit stood at Rs 18.1 crore during the quarter.
On a half-yearly basis, the company's revenue from operations grew 51.70% to Rs 268 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 177 crore in H1 FY26. Its profit before tax stood at Rs 28.5 crore during the first half of FY27.
RentoMojo made its stock market debut in September this year at a 19% premium over its IPO price. The listing followed strong investor demand for its Rs 1,256 crore IPO, which was subscribed 72.87 times.
RentoMojo's shares are currently trading at around Rs 615 per share (as of 14:42), giving the company a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 6,459 crore. This is around 52% above its IPO issue price of Rs 404 per share.

title: Kutumb parent posts Rs 405 Cr total income in FY26; profit surges 6X
summary:
Bengaluru-based Primetrace Technologies, the company behind consumer apps such as Kutumb, Crafto AI, Tarot AI, Sundar AI and Polo, had a strong FY26, with its revenue tripled and net profit jumped nearly sixfold during the year.
Primetrace's revenue from operations surged to Rs 386 crore in FY26 from Rs 123 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
The company operates a portfolio of consumer-focused apps, including Kutumb and Crafto. It follows a freemium business model, offering free access to core features while generating revenue primarily through subscriptions, advertising and user-paid digital services across its platforms. The sale of these services was the company's sole source of operating revenue.

Besides operating revenue, Primetrace earned Rs 19 crore from interest on other current investments, taking its total income to Rs 405 crore in FY26 from Rs 138 crore in FY25.
Advertising emerged as its largest cost head, accounting for nearly 75% of the overall expenditure. The company spent Rs 273 crore on advertising in FY26, a 3.3X increase from Rs 82 crore in the previous fiscal year. This spending is crucial for consumer app businesses looking to build awareness and acquire users across platforms.
Employee benefit expenses grew 26.2% to Rs 33.5 crore, while information technology, legal, travel and other overheads also contributed to the rise in costs. Overall, the company's expenditure increased 2.7X to Rs 363 crore in FY26 from Rs 135 crore in FY25.

On a unit economics basis, the company spent Rs 0.94 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 9.8% and 6.55%, respectively. At the end of the fiscal year, its current assets stood at Rs 218 crore.

Primetrace has raised around $30 million to date, with Peak XV Partners and Tiger Global among its investors. Building a business with nearly Rs 400 crore in operating revenue while remaining profitable, without raising substantial external capital, is commendable. The company is also reportedly in talks to raise another $50 million from 60 One Asset and other investors.
With multiple apps catering to different consumer needs, it will be interesting to see whether Primetrace can sustain this growth, improve its margins, and scale its portfolio further in the coming years.

title: Blue Tokai crosses Rs 500 Cr revenue in FY26; losses up 54%
summary:
Coffee chain Blue Tokai continued to expand its business in FY26, with revenue crossing the Rs 500 crore mark, supported by its presence in the organised cafe market. However, the expansion came with a higher cost burden, as losses widened 53.7% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Blue Tokai’s revenue from operations surged 59.4% to Rs 518 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 325 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


The company also reported Rs 7.5 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 525.5 crore during the last fiscal year.

Sales of coffee and related products remained Blue Tokai’s primary source of operating revenue, rising 59.3% to Rs 513 crore in FY26 from Rs 322 crore in FY25. Lease income increased 36.2% to Rs 3.5 crore, while revenue from services stood at Rs 1 crore during the fiscal year.
The increase in operating costs outpaced revenue growth, putting pressure on Blue Tokai’s profitability. The cost of materials consumed, its largest cost component, increased 65.5% to Rs 187 crore in FY26 from Rs 113 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 35.9% to Rs 130.5 crore, while rent expenses grew 59.6% to Rs 26.65 crore during the last fiscal year.
Depreciation costs nearly 2X jumped to Rs 87 crore. Finance costs also jumped 68.8% to Rs 27 crore from Rs 16 crore in the same period.
Other expenses grew 70.5% to Rs 150 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25, accounting for 25% of the total expenditure. Consequently, the Gurugram-based company's total expenses increased 61.7% to Rs 608 crore in FY26 from Rs 376 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the profitability front, Blue Tokai's EBITDA stood at Rs 23 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 19.4 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA margin declined to 4.44% from 5.97%. The company's net losses widened 53.7% to Rs 83 crore in FY26 from Rs 54 crore in the previous fiscal year.


Blue Tokai's return on capital employed (ROCE) stood -11.94% in FY26. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 1.17 to  earn a rupee in the same period.

The company's cash and bank balances declined to Rs 39 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 118 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, its total assets increased to Rs 697 crore from Rs 521 crore previous fiscal year.
Blue Tokai operates in an increasingly competitive coffee market, with Third Wave Coffee among its main rivals. Third Wave is yet to disclose its FY26 financial results, while Tata Starbucks reported operating revenue of Rs 1,367 crore and a 27% reduction in net losses during the year. 
The comparison highlights the gap in scale as Blue Tokai seeks to strengthen its position in India’s organised cafe market. Its next phase will depend on growing its store network while improving store-level economics, customer retention and op-efficiency. Building scale without adding proportionate costs will remain central to its path to profitability.

title: ShareChat parent crosses Rs 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26, posts Rs 672 Cr loss
summary:
It has been around 11 years since ShareChat started building its business around India's vernacular internet audience. The company has often been projected as a potential rival to Meta in India, but it is yet to give any meaningful competition to the social media giant. While ShareChat continues to experiment with new formats and has recently entered the microdrama segment to keep up with the trend, the business is still struggling to move towards profitability.
We are decoding its annual results for FY26. After two years of moderate growth in FY24 and FY25, ShareChat's revenue from operations grew 40.5% to Rs 1,016 crore in FY26 from Rs 723 crore in FY25.
Its parent company, Mohalla Tech, operates a vernacular social media and digital entertainment business through platforms such as ShareChat, Moj and QuickTV, targeting regional-language audiences in India.
Revenue from ShareChat's chatroom feature, where users can interact through video calls, accounted for 46% of its total operating revenue. This segment grew 8.8% to Rs 471 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, advertising revenue declined 13% to Rs 252 crore during the year.
On the other hand, QuickTV contributed Rs 293 crore in subscription revenue in FY26. Unlike advertising revenue, subscription revenue is recognised over the subscription period. The company also added Rs 89 crore through the reversal of provisions for doubtful assets, taking its total income to Rs 1,105 crore.

As the company continues to push its new business verticals, its business development expenses surged 8.7X to Rs 335 crore in FY26 from Rs 43 crore in FY25. Following layoffs over the past year, employee benefit expenses declined 16% to Rs 220 crore. We have excluded ESOP expenses of Rs 739 crore and Rs 184 crore in FY26 and FY25, respectively, from this comparison, as these are non-cash expenses.
The company also spent Rs 549 crore on interest expenses against its borrowings through debt securities. Server costs, content development, legal and other overheads pushed its overall expenses up 14.6% to Rs 1,777 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,550 crore in FY25.
While QuickTV has added a new revenue stream to the business, it is yet to translate into meaningful improvement in profitability. Mohalla Tech's net loss, however, narrowed 15.58% to Rs 672 crore in FY26 from Rs 796 crore in FY25.
We have not excluded ESOP expenses and unrealised foreign exchange losses while calculating the overall losses to give a fair picture of the company's financial performance. On a unit level, Mohalla Tech spent Rs 1.75 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, while its EBITDA margin stood at -84%.
Yes, ShareChat and Moj together have a user base of over 300 million, and with such a large audience, QuickTV could turn out to be a big opportunity for the company if it gets things right. However, the decline in advertising revenue also raises questions about whether brands are finding the right audience on its platforms or shifting their preference elsewhere. Even the chatroom segment, which contributes the largest share of revenue, is growing at a moderate pace. The next couple of years will be quite important for Mohalla Tech as it tries to build new revenue streams, make better use of its existing user base and, more importantly, move towards profitability.

title: Festive boost: D2C startups bag every third funding deal in October
summary:
Indian startup funding witnessed a sharp slowdown in October, but consumer-focused brands showed resilience. D2C startups raised around $200 million during the month, which was nearly 30% of the total $678 million raised by Indian startups.
In terms of deal volume, D2C startups accounted for 36 of the 108 deals recorded in October, which was 33.33% of the total. Their share was higher than the 20.36% recorded in H1 2026, when they secured 125 of the 614 deals, and 21.57% in Q3 2026, with 55 deals out of 255. This points to a growing share of consumer focused brands in India's startup funding activity.
In terms of deal value, D2C startups raised a little over $1 billion during the first nine months of 2026, which accounted for around 10% of the more than $10 billion raised by Indian startups during the period.
The strong showing by consumer brands comes at an important time as companies prepare for the festive and wedding seasons, when consumer spending typically picks up. For these startups, fresh capital could help them build inventory, expand distribution, strengthen supply chains and increase marketing spend to capture a larger share of the market.
According to Entrackr's funding data, consumer focused startups attracted investments across categories such as fashion, beauty, food, wellness, lifestyle and home products.


Food and beverages emerged as the largest category with eight deals, followed by fashion and lifestyle and health and wellness, which attracted seven deals each. Home and living brands secured six deals, while beauty and personal care companies accounted for four deals. Together, these five categories represented 32 of the 36 D2C funding deals recorded during the month, accounting for nearly 89% of the total.
Sports and fitness brand Boldfit topped the list with a $42 million Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund. Design led lifestyle brand DailyObjects followed with a $35 million Series C round, backed by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Asia Private Capital.
Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit raised $15 million in a Series C round led by Trident Growth Partners, while men's bottomwear brand The Pant Project secured $11.5 million in a Series B round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment.
Food and consumer brands also attracted investor interest. Troovy raised $10.5 million in a Series B round led by Sharrp Ventures. Beyond Appliances, a smart kitchen technology company, also secured $11.5 million from Fireside Ventures.
Several other consumer brands raised capital during the month. These included Ace Blend ($9.91 million), MakeO ($9.5 million), Rotoris ($7.4 million), ChapterHome ($6.4 million), Kisah ($3.7 million), SuperMush ($3 million), The Stack ($2.2 million), Gramiyaa ($2 million). Smaller rounds also came from brands such as Lorazzo, Bangalore Watch Company, ReplyAll, So/Facet, Zinara, ISLAND Beauty and Qiroko.
The timing of these investments is particularly relevant. The festive season is one of the biggest opportunities for consumer brands to improve sales, acquire new customers and build market share.
Beyond tracking the growth of India's consumer brands, Entrackr is also looking to build a stronger founder community through The Spur – The D2C Mixer. The idea is to bring D2C founders together in an informal setting where they can step away from their everyday business routines, meet peers, exchange experiences and have meaningful conversations. As these brands continue to scale, a community where founders can connect, learn from each other's journeys and share challenges becomes equally important. The Spur is an effort to create that space, without panels, pitches or formal presentations. The focus remains on genuine conversations and long term connections.
The opportunity ahead is also significant. According to IBEF, India's D2C market is projected to reach $60 billion by 2030. A separate estimate by NeoMa Capital puts the total addressable market (TAM) for D2C brands at around $100 billion in FY26, including online and offline consumer discretionary spending. However, the currently obtainable market through brand websites and direct channels is estimated at $25 billion. This highlights the headroom for homegrown consumer brands to expand their presence and capture a larger share of India's growing consumption market.
D2C startups are an important part of India's startup ecosystem. They bring a certain charm to the ecosystem through new brands, products that reach consumers and challenges to established players across categories. The next few years could see many more homegrown brands emerge, scale and become household names. title: PhysicsWallah cites AI efficiencies for job cuts; offline biz faces profit pressure, earmarks $20 Mn for M&A
summary:
Edtech company PhysicsWallah is using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiencies and reduce its workforce requirements, even as it looks to expand through inorganic route — acquisitions. The Noida-based company also continues to face profitability challenges in its offline business, despite the expansion of its Vidyapeeth centres.
During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management confirmed that its total employee count, which stood at around 19,100, and faculty strength of approximately 7,100 declined sequentially in the quarter. The firm attributed the reduction partly to efficiencies from AI across content creation, quality checks, test paper preparation and evaluation.
Management said AI now writes around 90% of the company's code. The shift towards automation has also helped contain employee expenses, which declined 2.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, excluding ESOP costs. For the first half of FY27, employee expenses were down 2.4% compared to the same period last year.
However, PhysicsWallah continues to invest in technology which stood at Rs 104 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 70 crore in the corresponding period last year.
While AI-led efficiencies have helped improve operating leverage, PhysicsWallah's offline business remains a key area to watch. The segment reported a pre-Ind AS EBITDA loss of Rs 108 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 120 crore in the year-ago period, as per figures discussed during the call.
The offline business reported 9% year-on-year revenue growth to Rs 541 crore in Q2 FY27, while H1 revenue rose 12% to Rs 1,031 crore. Management attributed the moderation in growth partly to lower NEET enrolments and delays in government exam notifications, which affected demand at some of its centres.

PhysicsWallah operates 370 offline centres, including 167 Vidyapeeth centres, compared to 117 in the previous year. Vidyapeeth contributed around 66% of the company's offline business collections in H1 FY27. Management said the standalone Vidyapeeth business is already profitable and expects the broader offline segment to move closer to breakeven. The company plans to add 25-30 offline centres annually over the next two to three years, while keeping a tighter check on upfront costs.
Alongside its focus on operational efficiency, PhysicsWallah is also evaluating acquisitions to expand its online education biz. The company said it is in advanced discussions with a couple of fully online education businesses and is actively evaluating several other opportunities.
It has earmarked less than $20 million for these acquisitions, in line with the Rs 300 crore allocation from its IPO proceeds for unidentified acquisitions. Management expects the deals to be margin-accretive and said they could strengthen its presence in new categories while offering synergies with its technology and YouTube-led distribution.
PhysicsWallah's FY27 revenue growth guidance of around 30% includes the potential contribution from acquisitions. However, management expects M&A to contribute less than 5% to revenue growth during the year.
The company reported consolidated revenue of Rs 1,242 crore in Q2 FY27, which rose 18% year-on-year, while net profit rose to Rs 142 crore from Rs 70 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: FamApp’s revenue touches Rs 25 Cr in FY26, profit nosedives 99%
summary:
FamPay Solutions Private Limited, the entity behind fintech app FamApp, reported a 20.5% increase in revenue from operations and crossed the Rs 25 crore milestone in FY26. However, higher employee and other operating expenses sharply reduced its profit by 99%.
The Bengaluru-based company has reported a 20.5% increase in operating revenue to Rs 25.02 crore in FY26 from Rs 20.75 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
With Rs 5.01 crore in interest income and Rs 5.2 crore in gains from the sale of investments, its total income increased 13.1% to Rs 35.23 crore during the last fiscal year. It's important to note that the financials presented here are based on its standalone statements.

Expenses, meanwhile, grew 34.7% to Rs 35.18 crore, outpacing revenue growth. Employee benefit expenses increased 23.3% to Rs 16.16 crore, while other expenses rose 47.1% to Rs 18.45 crore. Its technical fees saw a jump of 82% to Rs 10.22 crore in FY26
Consequently, profit before tax fell to Rs 4.8 lakh in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 5.04 crore in the previous year.
The balance sheet showed cash and cash equivalents of Rs 61.83 crore as of March 2026, up from Rs 20.62 crore a year earlier. Current investments, however, declined to Rs 26.5 crore from Rs 54.6 crore. 
The financial performance comes amid changes in FamApp’s reset. In June 2025, Entrackr reported that Elevation Capital led a $15 million secondary round in the company, with a large part of the investment going towards purchasing shares held by co-founder Kush Taneja. Taneja subsequently exited the company.
FamApp’s financial performance points to a business at a critical stage of its evolution. The challenge now is to establish whether its revenue growth can support a more efficient operating model as it expands. The sharp erosion in profitability raises questions about the cost of scaling and the sustainability of its current economics. 
While its cash reserves provide room to invest in the business, the focus will need to shift towards improving operating leverage and building a more predictable earnings profile. It is important to note that these numbers reflect FamPay Solutions’ standalone performance and not the consolidated one. Its ability to balance growth with cost discipline will determine whether it can build a durable fintech business.

title: DriveU’s net profit doubles in FY26; NTV grows to Rs 131 Cr
summary:
India’s mobility market is largely dominated by ride-hailing platforms such as Uber, Ola and Rapido, which connect consumers with taxis and two-wheeler services. However, a parallel market for on-demand drivers is emerging, particularly among car owners who seek a convenient alternative to driving themselves. Concerns around drunk driving and road safety have further fuelled demand for such services, creating opportunities for platforms such as DriveU, which allow customers to hire verified drivers to drive their own vehicles.
DriveU continued to scale its business while maintaining profitability for the third consecutive financial year. During the fiscal year ended March 2026, the company more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore, while its net revenue grew 14% year-on-year.
The Bengaluru-based company’s net revenue increased to Rs 32.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.9 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements.

Founded in 2015 by father-son duo Ashok Shastry and Rahm Shastry, DriveU offers trained, verified drivers on demand for customers’ own cars. It also operates DriveU Reserve, a premium cab service, and DriveU Coach, an at-home driving lessons platform. The company operates in 13 cities and has completed over 10.5 million trips with more than 100,000 registered driver-partners.
The company’s net transaction value (NTV) increased 17% to Rs 131 crore in FY26 from Rs 112 crore in the previous fiscal year. Its gross revenue stood at Rs 131 crore during the year.
On the expense side, DriveU paid around Rs 97.21 crore to driver-partners during FY26. Employee benefit expenses remained stable at Rs 13.7 crore.
Direct expenses, including partner incentives, technology costs and trip insurance, stood at Rs 8.35 crore. Meanwhile, business promotion and marketing expenses declined 5% year-on-year to Rs 4.84 crore. Overall, the company’s expenses grew 10% to Rs 30.5 crore during FY26.
On the profitability front, DriveU more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1.73 crore in FY25, maintaining profitability for the third consecutive year. Its EBITDA grew 58% year-on-year to Rs 2.74 crore, while the EBITDA margin on net revenue improved to 8.3% from 6% in the previous fiscal year.

As of March 2026, it had cash and bank balances of Rs 12 crore and total current assets of Rs 20 crore.
DriveU has raised a total of Rs 54 crore since its inception, with its last funding round taking place in 2024. The company has not raised any fresh capital since then.
Beyond its core driver-on-demand business, the company launched two new verticals in April 2026: DriveU Reserve, a chauffeur-driven premium cab service, and DriveU Coach, which provides driving lessons at customers’ homes.
The company expects its gross revenue to reach Rs 170 crore in FY27, representing a growth of around 30% over FY26. It plans to expand both Reserve and Coach into more cities, while funding investments in these businesses through operating cash flows.
